summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It leads the overall convergence ranking (score 4.5197) and is the only gene in the robust overall top ten. It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712), survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 7.787), and single-cell data place 0.976 of its tumour transcripts in RCC cells. Girentuximab reached PHASE_3. DepMap shows no dependency (mean effect 0.051), so its value lies in antibody, imaging or radioligand approaches and in diagnosis, not in essential-gene inhibition.

A second tier of tumour-up candidates is protein-confirmed, replicated in TCGA-KIRC and purity-robust: SCARB1 (top of the target profile), CD70, NNMT, SLC16A3 (MCT4), ENPP3 and HK2. CD70 and ENPP3 already have antibody or ADC programmes. NNMT adds adverse prognosis and supportive ccRCC literature. SCARB1 and ENPP3 have no ccRCC literature relations in the corpus. None of these genes is a selective DepMap dependency, so the target calls rest on tumour-restricted expression and tractability rather than on essentiality.

The biomarker profile is led by genes lost with proximal-tubule identity: PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, SLC6A19 and PPP1R1A, together with ALDOB and SLC22A8 in the overall ranking. They are down in tumour at RNA and protein, replicate in TCGA-KIRC and carry significant TCGA survival associations. That makes them diagnostic and prognostic candidates, not therapeutic targets.

The clinically validated ccRCC axes appear as context, not as data-led discoveries. VHL is the dominant somatic driver, EPAS1 (belzutifan, approved) is the only candidate with ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency, and KDR is an endothelial angiogenesis target. Discovery candidates (COL23A1 and RAB42 in tumour, OLFML2A and JAG2 in stroma, GAL3ST4 and LILRB4 in the immune track) are data-ranked hypotheses without dependency evidence.

omics.text: In CPTAC tumour-vs-normal data CA9 is the clearest up-regulated candidate: RNA log2FC 6.312 and protein log2FC 2.269, with a modest positive copy-number cis effect (rho 0.224).

Other tumour-up genes with protein confirmation are SCARB1 (RNA log2FC 2.974, protein 1.837), CD70 (RNA 4.464, protein 2.421), NNMT (RNA 4.67, protein 2.709), SLC16A3 (RNA 3.435, protein 2.279), ENPP3 (RNA 3.895, protein 1.544) and HK2 (RNA 3.351, protein 2.106).
FABP6 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921), and its copy number is gained in 0.573 of tumours with a cis effect of rho 0.309, a genuine dosage contribution.
On the loss side, ALDH6A1 is down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein (log2FC -1.925), with CNV loss frequency 0.355 and a positive cis effect (rho 0.525), consistent with a copy-loss dosage effect.

literature.text: Literature support is concentrated on CA9, CD70 and NNMT. CA9-targeted PET is described as proof-of-concept warranting prospective validation. CD70 is reported as overexpressed in RCC with minimal normal-tissue expression, a downstream HIF target, and the subject of 68Ga-labelled single-domain-antibody tracers. NNMT is described as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target, and selective tool inhibitors exist in a non-ccRCC chemistry paper.

Most biomarker literature (ALDOB, SLC22A8, ENO2, FCER1G, PFKP, PLIN2) rests on single bioinformatic or IHC studies without prospective validation. COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) has the densest mechanistic literature (HIF induction, glycolysis, ferroptosis) but is preclinical. The corpus also contains contradictions: MT1G is low in tumour yet high MT1G is linked to poor prognosis, and PFKP is up in tumour while low PFKP is linked to poor survival. SCARB1, ENPP3 and EPAS1 have no extracted ccRCC literature relations despite strong data or clinical support.

external.text: Open Targets drug records separate candidates with clinical programmes from untested ones. CA9 (girentuximab, PHASE_3), CD70 (vorsetuzumab mafodotin, PHASE_1) and ENPP3 (AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2) are membrane proteins accessible to antibodies. NNMT and SCARB1 have predicted tractability only and no drugs listed.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target with belzutifan approved. DepMap shows a selective but partial dependency (selectivity 0.3, fraction of ccRCC lines dependent 0.208, padj 0.061), and it is not common essential.
VHL is the core driver, mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.483). It has no drug of its own, so the therapeutic route is downstream HIF-2alpha.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of its tumour transcripts (54.7% of RCC cells express it), and tumour cells versus proximal tubule give log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189).

Several clinical candidates are microenvironmental rather than tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial (0.951 of transcripts), CD74 is carried mainly by macrophages (0.436), and CXCR4 by CD8 T cells (0.563). EPAS1 transcripts in this scRNA-seq dataset are mostly endothelial (0.365) rather than RCC (0.051). By contrast MET is mainly tumour-cell (0.935). CD70 single-cell records carried no evidence ids, so its cell-level split is not quoted; its purity-1 log2FC supports tumour-intrinsic expression.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are explained by RCC (composition-corrected share 0.999), and their ring-1 neighbours are enriched for RCC (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017; observed 0.4757 vs expected 0.3654). CA9 therefore marks tumour-cell-rich niches.

High-CD74 spots are explained mostly by macrophages (composition-corrected share 0.637, RCC 0.159), and their neighbours are enriched for T cells (log2 enrichment 0.388) and macrophages (0.218), an immune niche rather than a tumour-cell one.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank candidate sites; they are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (volume 126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, one accessible lysine), with ligand-site recall 0.5. That is a modest site for a protein already addressed by antibodies.
Among discovery candidates, RAB42 has the best-ranked site (score 0.5348, 37.4 A3, mean pLDDT 85.31, 3 accessible lysines), but the pocket is small and lacks ligand validation.
The COL23A1 model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91) with a single 8.0 A3 pocket scoring 0.2342, so it is not a credible degrader site.

discovery.text: The tumour-track discovery lead is COL23A1. It is novel in having no clinical drug, it is antibody or PROTAC tractable and surface or secreted, and its vital-organ expression is low (3 nTPM, heart muscle). RCC cells carry 0.881 of its transcripts. It replicates in TCGA (log2FC 5.829) and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (log2FC at purity 1 of 4.88). It shows no dependency (DepMap mean effect 0.167).

RAB42 is a second tumour-track hypothesis: RCC cells hold 0.627 of its transcripts, there is no clinical drug, vital-organ expression peaks at 2.6 nTPM (lung), and it replicates in TCGA (log2FC 4.371) with a purity-1 log2FC of 3.189. DepMap shows no dependency (-0.075).

The stroma track gives OLFML2A (fibroblast-borne, 0.647 of transcripts; TCGA log2FC 2.372, purity-1 log2FC 1.527; vital-organ expression 27.9 nTPM in colon) and JAG2 (mostly endothelial, 0.487; TCGA log2FC 1.549, purity-1 log2FC 1.061, Cox log HR -0.177). Both have modest effect sizes and no functional evidence.

The immune track is mostly infiltration. GAL3ST4 is macrophage-borne (0.972) with TCGA log2FC 2.993 but purity-1 log2FC only 0.401. LILRB4 (macrophage, 0.933) has TCGA log2FC 3.7 that falls to 0.508 at purity 1, so its bulk signal reflects macrophage abundance. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: External replication in TCGA-KIRC is strong for the leading targets: CA9 (log2FC 9.712), CD70 (7.09), ENPP3 (5.557), NNMT (4.685), SCARB1 (3.989) and SLC16A3 (3.291). All stay up when extrapolated to a pure tumour (purity-1 RNA log2FC 7.787, 4.278, 5.278, 5.256, 3.762 and 3.821), so these changes come from tumour cells rather than infiltration.

Prognosis strengthens NNMT: higher expression is adverse in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479), whereas CA9, CD70 and SCARB1 are not prognostic. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency for NNMT (mean effect 0.316, selectivity -0.075).

The independent layers weaken the essentiality case across the board. None of the top candidates is a recurrent somatic driver (VHL alone is, at frequency 0.483), and EPAS1 is the only selective DepMap dependency (selectivity 0.3). Infiltration-driven immune genes such as LILRB4 lose most of their bulk change at purity 1 (0.508).

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting, the target profile is stable at the top. SCARB1 (p_top10 0.968, rank interval 1 to 8), CA9 (0.941, 1 to 13), SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 and NNMT (0.88 each) and ENPP3 (0.823) form the robust target top ten. In the biomarker profile PSAT1 is the most stable call (p_top10 0.986, rank interval 1 to 4), followed by PCK1 (0.889) and SLC6A19 (0.881).

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is robustly top ten (p_top10 0.894). In the biomarker profile, DUSP9 (p_top10 0.398, with a 90% rank interval reaching beyond rank 100) and L1CAM (p_top10 0.297) are fragile, as are target-profile entries from rank 11 down, such as PNCK (p_top10 0.004).

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most fully on CA9 and CD70: both are tumour-intrinsic, protein-confirmed, TCGA-replicated, literature-backed and clinically addressed. NNMT converges on omics, literature and prognosis but lacks a drug. SCARB1, ENPP3, SLC16A3 and HK2 are data-led, with thin or absent ccRCC literature.

Disagreements are informative. The validated clinical axes (VHL, EPAS1, MTOR) score high in Open Targets but not in the omics convergence, and EPAS1 transcripts are mostly non-tumour in single-cell data. Down-regulated tubule-identity genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, PSAT1) top the overall and biomarker rankings but are biomarkers, not targets.

targets.rationale: Top overall convergence and target rank 2 with p_top10 0.941. Tumour-intrinsic by purity, single-cell and spatial data, replicated in TCGA, literature-backed for imaging, and girentuximab reached PHASE_3. No DepMap dependency, so this is an antibody, imaging and biomarker play.

Ranked above SCARB1 despite a lower target score because literature, clinical programmes (vorsetuzumab mafodotin, PHASE_1) and data agree. Up at RNA and protein, TCGA log2FC 7.09, purity-1 log2FC 4.278. Surface antigen for ADC, antibody or CAR-T, not a dependency.

Robust in both profiles (target p_top10 0.88). Tumour-intrinsic (purity-1 log2FC 5.256), adverse prognosis (Cox log HR 0.301), and literature calling it a prognostic biomarker and potential target. No drug yet.

Top of the target profile and the most robust target (p_top10 0.968). Up at RNA and protein, TCGA log2FC 3.989, purity-1 log2FC 3.762, with Open Targets genetic association 0.519. Placed fourth because it has no ccRCC literature and no drug.
Membrane ectoenzyme up at RNA and protein with TCGA log2FC 5.557, and the ADC AGS-16C3F reached PHASE_2. Robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.823). No ccRCC literature relations in the corpus.
MCT4 lactate transporter, target rank 3 (p_top10 0.881), up at RNA and protein, TCGA log2FC 3.291 and purity-1 log2FC 3.821. Metabolic rationale, but no drug and no dependency.

Included despite a modest convergence rank because it is the approved ccRCC target (belzutifan) and the only candidate with ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency (selectivity 0.3). Its transcripts are mainly non-tumour in single-cell data.
Most robust biomarker (p_top10 0.986). Down at RNA (log2FC -3.867) and protein, replicated in TCGA (log2FC -2.974), and prognostic (Cox log HR 0.43, padj 5.66e-7).
Down at RNA and protein with copy-loss dosage (cnv_loss_freq 0.355, cis rho 0.525). Strongest survival association among biomarkers (Cox log HR -0.554 for higher expression).
Gluconeogenic tubule-identity gene, down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein, replicated in TCGA (log2FC -3.079), protective when high (Cox log HR -0.415). Robust (p_top10 0.889).
Overall convergence rank 2, driven by loss: TCGA log2FC -4.741 and purity-1 log2FC -6.302, with literature describing it as a prognostic biomarker. A biomarker, not a target.
Proximal-tubule transporter down at RNA (log2FC -4.574), replicated in TCGA (log2FC -3.221), favourable when high (Cox log HR -0.456). Robust biomarker call (p_top10 0.881).

limitations.text: No leading candidate is a selective DepMap dependency except EPAS1, so target calls rest on tumour-restricted expression and tractability, not on demonstrated essentiality.
Down-regulated biomarkers largely reflect loss of proximal-tubule identity and partly reflect tissue composition. Their diagnostic value needs prospective validation.
Literature coverage is uneven: SCARB1, ENPP3, VHL and EPAS1 have no extracted ccRCC relations, and much biomarker literature consists of single bioinformatic studies.
Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank structural sites only; no degrader is shown to exist, and small pockets or poor AlphaFold models weaken several sites.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses with no functional or dependency evidence; literature is counted by gene symbol.
This is a replicate run (runs/replicates/rep1) used to measure run-to-run variability. Agents did not query every per-gene tool (e.g. phosphosites, kinase activity, STRING).
